parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: A distant star is orbited by several planets. Each planet has a circular orbit with a different radius.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Each planet orbits at constant speed.
Explain whether the planets are in equilibrium.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.stem:
The radius of the orbit of a planet is $R$ and the orbital period is $T$.

Data for some of the planets are given in Fig. 1.1.

| {{header}} planet | {{header}} $R / \text{m}$ | {{header}} $T^2 / \text{s}^2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| c | $9.6 \times 10^{10}$ | $2.5 \times 10^{11}$ |
| e | $4.0 \times 10^{11}$ | $1.8 \times 10^{13}$ |
| g | $2.1 \times 10^{12}$ | $2.6 \times 10^{15}$ |

Fig. 1.1

The relationship between $R$ and $T$ is given by the expression
$$R^3 = kT^2.$$

parts.text:
Show that the constant $k$ is given by the expression
$$k = \frac{GM}{4\pi^2}$$
where $G$ is the gravitational constant and $M$ is the mass of the star.
Use data from Fig. 1.1 for the three planets and the expression for $k$ to calculate the mass $M$ of the star.
